asn1::encode() has two strictnesses. strict (default) runs asn1c's constraint check first, which admits only the root of an extensible constraint: for values we build, an out-of-root value is a bug. relay leaves it to the PER encoder, which still refuses a value outside a non-extensible constraint and writes an extensible one's extension value with the extension bit: for re-encoding what was received (a newer peer's extension value) and for ksim-codec

NAS corpus (plan M11). One table-driven decoder for 5GMM and 5GSM (TS 24.007 11; tables generated by tools/nasgen.py from spec/nas). The header octets are the first mandatory V IEs; a half-octet pair takes the IE listed first in bits 4-1; the non-imperative part goes by IEI in any order. Error handling as TS 24.501 7.5-7.7 asks of a decoder: a short or missing mandatory part, or an unknown IE encoded as comprehension required (TS 24.007 11.2.4: type 4 with bits 8-5 zero, type 6 0x7E/0x7F), is an error; other unknown IEs are skipped by the format the IEI implies and kept; repeated IEs (7.6.3) and optional IEs outside their length range (7.7) are marked, not rejected, for the entity to ignore. Everything is kept as received, so encode(decode(x)) == x

NAS IE contents are octets in P0. Below the IEI and length only the ePCO is read, at container level (TS 24.008 10.5.6.3: identifier, a one- or two-octet length by the direction's table, contents as octets). Typed IE accessors, ePCO contents and the payload container's inner messages come with the entities in P1. The 9 messages outside v1 (the three NSSAA messages, the five relay key and relay authentication messages, PDU SESSION AUTHENTICATION RESULT) decode by the same tables, and the table sweep test covers them, but no oracle checks them; 3 IE types appear only there (24.501 9.11.3.88 to 9.11.3.90)

M11 SMS check: CP, RP and TPDU each round-trip; every element pycrate (TS24011_PPSMS, TS23040_SMS) reads holds what ours read; tshark reads CP as gsm_a_dtap and RP as gsm_a_rp, and a TPDU inside an RP-DATA or RP-ACK built for its direction, because its dissector takes the direction from the RP layer (TS 23.040 9.2.3.1). 29 checks, all PASS

TPDU decoding takes the direction, since TP-MTI alone does not name the type (TS 23.040 9.2.3.1), and for a report whether the carrying RP message is an RP-ERROR (TP-FCS present, 9.2.2.1a, 9.2.2.2a). TP-PI follows 9.2.3.27: a further TP-PI octet while bit 8 is set; a reserved bit set announces octets after TP-UD, which are kept as discarded rather than rejected; TP-UDL without TP-DCS means the default alphabet. GSM 7-bit packing follows TS 23.038 6.1.2.1, with fill bits after a user data header; a character outside the default alphabet and its extension table is an error, not a substitution

Oracle limits seen in M12. pycrate 0.8.1 misreads a chain of GTP-U extension headers: it reads every header as the first one's type and loses the next types and the PSC's QFI (OCUDU's Error Indication with a PSC and a UDP Port header, and its G-PDU with PDCP PDU Number and PSC), so it is not consulted for a PDU with more than one extension header. pycrate 0.8.1 and tshark 4.6.4 lack the Rel-17 IEs GTP-U Tunnel Status Information (230) and Recovery Time Stamp (231): pycrate keeps the first such IE and stops, tshark calls it an unknown extension header; and tshark 4.6.4 does not dissect a Tunnel Status message (253) at all. Each is matched by a rule that names it (ORACLE_LAG); Tunnel Status is checked by our round trip and pycrate's header reading only. tshark's nrup shows no BSSize, TTNB, new IE flags or retransmission fields, which are therefore not compared

Corpus (plan M12): 14 GTP-U PDUs from OCUDU's tests (gtpu_test_shared.h, gtpu_tunnel_nru_test.cpp), 4 of the 7 types; two arrays that are not GTP-U PDUs (the inner IP packet, a PDCP PDU) are excluded by shape (version 1, PT 1, Length covering the rest). TS 38.415 j10 figure 5.5.2.1-1 puts the Rel-18 BSSI and TTNBI flags in the octet that carries PPI, which is present '0 or 1' times while only PPP announces it. The reading chosen: the octet is present when PPP is set, so BSSize and TTNB can only be signalled with a PPI. tshark 4.6.4 reads PPI the same way and has no BSSize or TTNB field; no other oracle reads them yet

GTP-U keeps the header as received (spare bit, and the optional part's fields whose flag is clear, which 5.1 says not to evaluate), the extension chain by type with contents as octets, and IEs by Table 8.1-1 (TV of fixed length, TLV with a two-octet length, the Extension Header Type List with a one-octet count; an unknown TV IE cannot be skipped and is an error). The PSC and NR-U frames are one table-driven reader and writer: each field names the flag bit that announces it, some fields are further flag octets, some are a count of fixed-size blocks; what follows the last field is kept, and a built frame is padded to 4n-2 octets

Kept small in P0: NR-U ASSISTANCE INFORMATION DATA (PDU type 2) is not in the frame tables (decode says unsupported); the contents of extension headers other than the PSC and NR RAN Container (RAN and Xw RAN Container, UDP Port, PDU Set Information) and of the GTP-U IEs stay octets; the PDCP PDU numbers are read and written from P3 R1 (KS-GTPU-B4). Timer wheel: against a plain reference model (a map by deadline and sequence) on 20 seeds of 4000 random schedules, cancels and advances with delays from overdue to 20,000 s, callbacks that cancel others and schedule follow-ups: the same firing order; next_deadline() equal to the model's after each of 20,000 operations; exact next deadlines on every level and in the overflow list (60 days); a stale handle cancels nothing. MPSC inbox under TSan: 10^8 messages from 4 producers to one consumer, every message once and each producer's in order, no report, 35.4 s and 36 MB on the dev PC (KSIM_MPSC_STRESS; CI runs 2x10^6 in every preset). The shard: tasks from 4 threads run on its thread, a cancelled timer never fires, a timer is never early, under TSan too

C++ pcapng writers read by tshark 4.6.4 on stdin: a capture with an Exported-PDU nas-5gs record, a GTP-U Echo Request in IPv4/UDP to 2152 and a GSMTAP-SIM SELECT on 4729 decodes as exported_pdu:nas-5gs, ip:udp:gtp and gsmtap:gsm_sim with no complaint, the nanosecond timestamp and the packet comment intact; a damaged closing block length makes tshark refuse the file (the must-fail case). The Exported-PDU tag pads the dissector name to 4 octets and counts the padding, as the M8 Python writer does

Runtime design (architecture §5) as built in M13. The timer wheel has four levels of 256 one-millisecond slots (2^32 ms) and an overflow list; advance() jumps to the next tick where a slot fires or a non-empty slot cascades, so hours of timers cost no idle ticks; a handle carries a generation and a fired or cancelled timer's node is released before its callback runs. The inbox is a bounded ring with per-cell sequence numbers (lock-free MPSC); post() fails when full, and only the post that finds no wake pending writes the eventfd. The shard runs at most a ring's worth of tasks per wake, so timers and descriptors are not starved, brings the wheel up to the clock before any task runs, and arms the timerfd for the wheel's next deadline only; its start_timer() counts a delay from the clock, not from the wheel's last advance, so a timer is never early (the M13 CI run under TSan caught a 30 ms timer firing 1 ms early through the wheel's own schedule_in). The log façade formats with fmt and cannot format SecretBytes (a static_assert); quill can replace its sink later

RP-Destination Address in an MO RP-DATA (L7). TS 24.011 j00 gives two bounds: Table 7.5 lists the element as LV of 1-12 octets (so a length octet of 0-11), while 8.2.5.2 says that in the mobile station to network direction the length octet is at least 2 and at most 11. The sim follows 8.2.5.2, the clause that states the direction: RP-DA is the service centre address from EF.SMSP (TS 31.102 4.2.27, TS-Service Centre Address), its length octet 2-11; a card whose EF.SMSP holds no service centre address makes the UE refuse the MO submission locally (an event and exit code 6) instead of sending an empty RP-DA, which is what UERANSIM does (kaluza-core SMS-SC14 relays such an RP-DATA leniently). kaluza-core's own decoder bounds the length octet 2-11 too (its SMS-C08), so both sides read 8.2.5.2 alike

summary: Runtime II as built in P1 N1 (ADR 0009 points 5 and 6). Executor (post, start_timer, stop_timer, now) is implemented by the real-time Shard and by SimLoop, a single-threaded virtual-time loop that runs posted tasks in order and otherwise jumps to the wheel's next deadline, firing by (deadline, scheduling order) as a Shard does; one conformance suite runs on both. Entities see only its TimerService half (R4). Rng is counter-based and keyed by (seed, key path): a stream's n-th value is SplitMix64's finaliser over key + n times the golden ratio, so streams never perturb each other and a run is a pure function of its seed (100 seeds, each run twice, alike; no two seeds alike). Yaml wraps yaml-cpp with strict scalars (only true/false; decimal or 0x integers with range checks), unknown-key refusal, and errors naming file:line:column and the path. EventRing numbers events in a bounded ring, long-polls with wait(), and calls its NDJSON listener under its lock so lines stay in seq order; event names are consteval literals that check_events.py ties to src/api/events.tsv. KSIM_MUTANT(name) is constant false unless built with KSIM_MUTATIONS=ON (preset mutants) and the process names the mutant in KSIM_MUTANT; check_mutants.py ties the sites to tests/mutants.tsv and its rows to gates/rows/p1.tsv. coro.hpp gives lazy Task<T>, spawn, CancelSource/CancelToken, sleep_for and a single-consumer Mailbox with a timeout; all resume inline on the actor's thread, so cancelling in an actor's destructor ends its procedures before its state goes (200 random cancel/expiry races: each waiter ends once, as expected, with no timer or frame left)

Virtual time measured (P1 N1): ten hours of a NAS timer model (T3512 54 min, T3502 12 min, the 10-15 s timers, T3346 random; a fifth of the timers stopped early and restarted) for 1000 UEs fire over 10,000 timers, each exactly at its deadline, in 18 ms on the dev PC's debug build (the release build asserts under 100 ms; sanitizer builds under 5 s). The whole platform suite (71 tests) passes in the dev, asan, tsan and release presets

Transports as built in P1 N2 (ADR 0009; architecture §5). platform/transport.hpp defines the ports protocol code uses: IAssoc (SCTP-like: send with stream and PPID, up, negotiated stream counts, shutdown, abort; events up, restart, shutdown, lost, refused), IDatagram and IStream, plus Endpoint (numeric IPv4/IPv6, prefix membership). memlink implements IAssoc and IDatagram in memory between executors: one hop is delay_ms plus a seeded jitter, a direction never reorders, deliveries to a destroyed end are dropped. net implements them over kernel sockets: SCTP one-to-one sockets through <linux/sctp.h> only (no libsctp): SCTP_INITMSG, SCTP_NODELAY, SCTP_RECVRCVINFO, SCTP_EVENT for ASSOC_CHANGE and SHUTDOWN_EVENT, SCTP_SNDINFO/SCTP_RCVINFO cmsgs with the PPID in network order, SCTP_STATUS for the negotiated streams, partial delivery reassembled up to a bound, sends queued on EAGAIN, BINDX_ADD and CONNECTX for several addresses. A stream at or above the negotiated count is refused (L10). SctpClient re-associates after a loss or refusal with a doubling backoff (L11; TS 38.412 §7). UDP reads in recvmmsg batches of 64 and drops (counted) what the kernel will not take; TCP queues writes. One conformance suite runs on memlink in virtual time, memlink across two shards and SCTP over loopback (whole 100 KB messages, per-stream order, the stream bound, graceful shutdown, abort as lost), plus reconnect after a server restart and retry while refused; 30 repetitions clean, 10 under TSan. A handler may shut down or abort an association but must not destroy it

The soft card as built in P1 N3 (sim-uicc.md sections 2-7). The card OS takes command APDUs and answers response APDUs with T=0 semantics on by default: a command without Le whose answer has data gets 61xx and GET RESPONSE; a wrong Le gets 6Cxx; GSM-class 'A0' commands get 6E00. Access rules are evaluated in the expanded format (AM_DO then SC_DOs: always, never, a key reference, OR and AND templates) from the EF.ARR named in each file's '8B'. Key files (AF20) hold their contents as SecretBytes and are never read out; the EFs that hold session keys (4F03, 4F05) persist only in the sealed secrets file, never in the YAML image. The USIM application runs AUTHENTICATE with Milenage or TUAK from AF20 and the Annex C SQN check from AF30, both in sysmoISIM's layouts so one burn path serves soft and real cards. Card secrets (K, OPc, PINs, ADM1, sealed EFs) live in a file sealed with AES-256-GCM under a 32-octet KEK from a 0600 file; K and OPc of a sim-range IMSI derive as the first 16 octets of HMAC-SHA-256(master, label || IMSI). The terminal is the ME's side: power-on, EF.DIR to the USIM AID, reads sized from the FCP, AUTHENTICATE returning CK and IK as SecretBytes; APDU buffers that carried keys or PINs are wiped. Template cards/usim-5g.yaml: services 10 12 19 20 21 33 42 43 45 71 122 123 124 126 129 133, PIN1 disabled, SMSP centre +99900000, the null SUCI scheme, routing indicator 0000

GET IDENTITY (TS 31.102 7.5) in the SUCI context computes nothing on the card in P1: the template leaves service 125 off (the ME computes the SUCI, the null scheme until the user picks the Profile A/B key ids, decision D6), so the card answers 6985 as 7.5.1.1 requires; a card offering 125 also answers 6985 for now. Card-side SUCI (Profile A/B via the existing ECIES library) comes with the user's key-id decision
evidence: src/uicc/usim/usim.cpp Usim::get_identity; tests/unit/uicc_card Usim.Clause7_5; P1 N3

summary: The soft card under test in P1 N3: 34 tests (TS 102 221 clauses as APDUs, every TS 35.208 Milenage set and a TS 35.233 TUAK set through AUTHENTICATE APDUs, the SQN check with AUTS verified by our MILENAGE, sealed secrets, images, the terminal over the in-process transport in virtual time) pass in the dev, asan and tsan presets; fuzz_card ran 45,765 APDU streams in 60 s with no failure. The KAT sets' SQNs are arbitrary 48-bit values, which the delta check rightly refuses against a fresh card, so those tests switch the delta check off; the lab cores start subscribers' SQNs low

Typed NAS IEs as built in P1 N4 (closes KS-NAS-G1 for P1). src/codec/nas/ie/ie.hpp gives each IE that P1's procedures build or interpret a struct with kRef (its clause), decode() over the IE's contents and encode(): 64 of the 164 IE types the 39 P1 messages use (5GS mobile identity with the null SUCI, 5G-GUTI, 5G-S-TMSI and IMEISV; TAI lists of all three types; NSSAI, rejected NSSAI; registration result, update type, registration and de-registration types; the authentication parameters; NAS security algorithms and ngKSI; UE security capability; the PSI bitmaps; QoS rules with every fixed-length packet filter component, QoS flow descriptions, PDU address, session-AMBR in bits per second; the GPRS timers in milliseconds; the ePCO DNS and MTU contents). Six are framed by the generic codec; the other 94 stay raw, each with its reason, in src/codec/nas/ie/p1_ies.tsv, which the guard check_nas_ies.py checks against the extracted message tables. A decoder refuses what its clause makes impossible and reads what the clause says to read as another value (an unused registration result as 3GPP access, an unknown DRX value as not specified); a DNN label is 1 to 63 octets without a dot, total 100 (TS 23.003 9.1; found by fuzz_nas_ies)

The UE's 5G NAS security context as built in P1 N4 (TS 24.501 4.4.3, 4.4.4.2, 4.4.6; TS 33.501 6.4, Annex A.8). Keys: K_NASint and K_NASenc from K_AMF for the selected algorithms; 5G-EA3/IA3 refused (KS-SEC-G1) and 5G-IA0 refused outside emergency. COUNT: 24 bits (overflow 16, SQN 8), 32 with leading zeros as input; the uplink COUNT is the next one used and wraps through the overflow counter; the downlink COUNT is the largest that verified, and a received COUNT is estimated from the SQN as always above it, so a replay fails its MAC and is discarded without changing state (4.4.3.2). Integrity covers octet 7 onwards; ciphering the message from octet 8; BEARER is the NAS connection identifier, 0x01 for 3GPP access (built as 0 until P1 N8: KS-SEC-D2); DIRECTION 0 up, 1 down. Before secure exchange only the messages of 4.4.4.2 are processed plain (IDENTITY REQUEST for the SUCI, AUTHENTICATION REQUEST/RESULT/REJECT, REGISTRATION REJECT except #76/#78/#81/#82, DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT, SERVICE REJECT except #76/#78); after it none. The initial message split keeps only the 4.4.6 cleartext IEs

An independent check of NAS protection (P1 N4): for K 000102..0f, OPc f0e0..00, RAND 0011..ff, SQN 000000000021, AMF 8000 and SUPI 001010000300001, K_AMF, K_NASint and K_NASenc came from tests/oracles/keychain.py (our pure-Python reading of TS 33.501 Annex A, independent of the C++), and the MACs and ciphertexts from the Python cryptography package's AES-CMAC (128-NIA2) and AES-CTR (128-NEA2). The context reproduces all four messages byte for byte (recomputed with BEARER 1 in P1 N8, KS-SEC-D2): an uplink SECURITY MODE COMPLETE (header type 4, COUNT 0), a downlink SECURITY MODE COMMAND (type 3, COUNT 0), a ciphered downlink message (type 2, COUNT 1) and a downlink message at COUNT 257 after the overflow counter's estimate. fuzz_nas_ies ran 14.7 million inputs in 120 s clean after the DNN fix

The core stub (tests/corestub, P1 N5; ADR 0009 point f) judges procedures, not encodings. It plays the AMF's NAS side and the home functions with kaluza-sim's own codecs and crypto: authentication vectors from the test subscriber's K and OPc with Milenage (SQN = SEQ || a five-bit IND of 0, AMF 8000), RES*/XRES*, K_AUSF, K_SEAF and K_AMF from the KAT-backed key chain, re-synchronisation from AUTS with MAC-S over a zero AMF (TS 33.102 6.3.3, 6.3.5). Each uplink message is checked against the spec (mandatory IEs, protection and header type, the uplink COUNT advancing by one, the MAC, and what the procedure requires of its content: null-scheme SUCI output = MSIN, cleartext-only initial message, RES* = XRES*, the failure cause the challenge calls for, IMEISV exactly when asked, the whole REGISTRATION REQUEST in the container) and recorded with its clause. A shared misreading of an encoding would pass here; encodings are judged by tshark and pycrate on run pcaps and by the two real cores

The UE's 5GMM entity as built in P1 N5 (src/proc/ue/nas_mm). Choices: (1) until N12 brings the protected initial message (4.4.6), an initial registration starts without a 5G NAS security context (ngKSI 7, cleartext IEs only, the whole message after the SMC), with the 5G-GUTI as identity when one is held; (2) the ME checks the AMF separation bit before the USIM sees the challenge, so a non-5G challenge (#26) costs no SQN; (3) on a third consecutive failed challenge (5.4.1.3.7) the UE releases locally without sending that third AUTHENTICATION FAILURE; (4) a SECURITY MODE COMMAND naming the current K_AMF keeps the COUNTs (4.4.3.1), so a replayed command fails its MAC; one after 5G AKA starts at 0; (5) the UE offers 5G-EA0-2 and 128-5G-IA1-2 (KS-SEC-G1: no EA3/IA3) and refuses 5G-IA0 and anything it did not offer with #24; (6) 24.501 messages N5 does not handle yet get 5GMM STATUS #97 (7.4); (7) reject causes #3, #6, #7, #11, #12, #13, #15 and #27 end in their own states; the others are 5.5.1.2.7 d until N12 (forbidden lists, T3346, #62); (8) a switch-off goes to 5GMM-NULL as soon as the request is sent

5GMM procedure tests in virtual time (tests/procedure, P1 N5): 24 tests named by clause, the UE's 5GMM entity and its personalised soft card against the core stub, each passing only with no failed stub verdict: initial registration with a null SUCI through 5G AKA, NIA2/NEA2 SMC with IMEISV and the container, accept and complete; #20, #21 with AUTS and resync, #26; three failed challenges and T3520 expiry (network failed, local release); the stored RES* for a repeated RAND without the USIM; AUTHENTICATION REJECT taken only with T3520 running (5.4.1.3.7 m); #23 for altered replayed capabilities, #24 for 5G-IA0; a plain accept after the SMC discarded; five T3510 attempts then T3502 (115 s of virtual time) and the counter reset on its expiry; rejects #7 and #111; normal and switch-off de-registration; T3521 four retransmissions then abort at 75 s; 5GMM STATUS #97. The state table matches the UE states extracted from 24.501 j80 5.1.3.2.1 (spec/nas/24501/mm_states_ue.tsv, docx_tables.py 1.2). In the mutants preset both N5 mutants are killed: null_suci_full_imsi (the stub's MSIN check) and kamf_input_sbi_spelling (the SMC fails its MAC)

Typed RRC builders and readers as built in P1 N6 (src/codec/asn1/msg/rrc). A message is a plain struct; encode() checks its inputs, builds the value as X.697 JSON and lets the generated asn1c code produce strict UPER (JER in, so every ASN.1 constraint is applied by the same code that decodes); readers decode UPER, render JER and read the fields P1 interprets. The JSON is nlohmann ordered_json because asn1c's JER decoder (mouse07410 18e56503) requires SEQUENCE members in definition order and rejects a value whose keys are sorted; it reads hex in either case. A fixed-size BIT STRING is the hex of its left-aligned octets. Covered: MIB, SIB1 (cell access info, UE timers), Paging, RRCSetupRequest, RRCSetup, RRCReject, SecurityModeCommand/Complete/Failure, RRCReconfiguration (radio bearers, masterCellGroup, NAS list) and its Complete, RRCRelease, UECapabilityEnquiry/Information, DL/ULInformationTransfer, CellGroupConfig (RLC bearers only) and a generic UE-NR-Capability

oracle.py builders (P1 N6, in tools/ci.d/50-oracles.sh): the 21 builder samples of tests/unit/asn1/rrc_samples.hpp, one per builder and variant, each PASS: pycrate 0.8.1 decodes and re-encodes them to the same value, tshark 4.6.4 dissects them with no expert error (the nested NAS PDUs included), and asn1c decodes, re-encodes byte for byte and gives the JER of pycrate's value. A first sample nesting a truncated NAS message was flagged by tshark and corrected

The UE's RRC entity as built in P1 N6 (src/proc/ue/rrc), owning its L2. Choices: (1) fixed camping (A-12): a MIB not barred and a SIB1 listing the selected PLMN; T300 from SIB1, else 1000 ms; (2) the establishment cause is mo-Signalling until N12 passes the NAS cause down; registeredAMF and the NSSAI in RRCSetupComplete wait for N12; (3) a random access problem ends the setup at once, as T300 would (TS 38.331 5.3.3.7); (4) AS security: K_RRCint, K_RRCenc, K_UPint and K_UPenc from the NAS's K_gNB (TS 33.501 A.8), the SecurityModeCommand's MAC-I verified from the PDCP PDU kept for it, integrity on both directions at once, ciphering on both after the SecurityModeComplete is submitted; NIA0 refused unless the D1 bisect switch is set, 128-NIA3/NEA3 refused (KS-SEC-G1); (5) RRCReconfiguration's NAS list goes up after the RRCReconfigurationComplete is out; a reconfiguration with bearers before AS security, or one the UE cannot follow, takes it to RRC_IDLE (A-13); (6) an SRB integrity failure releases (A-13)

UE RRC procedure tests in virtual time (tests/procedure/rrc_ue_test.cpp, P1 N6), 14 against a scripted gNB that plays the DU's MAC and the CU's RRC over gNB-side PDCP with the same builders: camping only on an unbarred cell of the selected PLMN; setup through random access carrying the NAS message (a random value, or Part1/Part2 of the 5G-S-TMSI); T300 and RRCReject as failures the NAS sees; AS SMC with NIA2/NEA2 whose SecurityModeComplete travels in the clear between header and MAC-I, then ciphered and verified traffic both ways; a command under a different K_gNB failing its integrity check (SecurityModeFailure); NIA0 refused; reconfiguration adding SRB2 and a DRB with SDAP headers, NAS forwarded after the complete, user data both ways through SDAP and an integrity-protected, ciphered DRB; bearers before AS security, release, capability enquiry, paging by 5G-S-TMSI and an SRB integrity failure. 5GMM's K_gNB equals the AMF's (TS 33.501 6.8.1.2.2: the SECURITY MODE COMPLETE's COUNT); mutant kgnb_wrong_ul_count is killed in the mutants preset

P3 R0 spike 2 (ADR 0013 point 13): a handover CellGroupConfig built through our JER route and read by two independent decoders (tools/spikes/cellgroup_ocudu.sh). tests/vectors/rrc/cellgroup-ho-spike.json is our DU's SRB1 bearer plus spCellConfig with reconfigurationWithSync: spCellConfigCommon (PCI 102, n78, SSB ARFCN 632628, 30 kHz, 106 PRBs, TDD pattern, ss-PBCH-BlockPower -16), newUE-Identity 17921, t304 ms1000, and contention-free RA on SSB 0 with preamble 63 (TS 38.331 §6.3.2). ksim-codec encoded it with asn1c's strict constraint check (56 octets). OCUDU's own decoder from the pinned tree (tools/ocudu_vectors/unpack.sh, new: ocudu-unpack linked against ~/kaluza-sim-peers/ocudu-d9d2263f4d's static libraries) unpacked it and packed the same octets again, reading recfg_with_sync present, t304 1000 ms, new UE id 17921, PCI 102, SSB ARFCN 632628 and CFRA present; pycrate decoded and re-encoded the same octets. Our DU's present CellGroupConfig and SIB1 also unpack and re-pack identically in OCUDU (t301 1000 ms, t311 3000 ms). OCUDU's CU-CP calls report_fatal_error on a target DU's CellGroupConfig or dedicated SIB1 it cannot unpack and reads t304, t301 and t311 from them (lib/cu_cp/routines/mobility/handover_reconfiguration_routine.cpp), so every RRC container we hand it is checked this way before a live run (R1)

PDCP security through the entity (P1 N6): the six 128-EEA2 sets of TS 33.401 Annex C (= 128-NEA2) go through a DRB PDCP entity with TX_NEXT at each set's COUNT and BEARER = RB identity - 1, and match over the whole octets of each set's LENGTH (sets 1 and 4-6 end mid-octet); the receiving entity deciphers them back. SRB1 PDUs with 128-NIA2 and 128-NEA2 (integrity over header and data, ciphering over data and MAC-I), a downlink SecurityModeCommand's MAC-I at COUNT 0, and a DRB whose SDAP header stays unciphered match vectors made with the Python cryptography package (AES-CMAC, AES-CTR)

KAIR v1 as built (src/codec/air, P1 N6; architecture.md 2.3): the 32-octet header and TLVs SDU (LCID, RLC mode, the SDU), MAC_CE, SCENE, CELL, PRACH, RAR, CONTENTION_ID and PAGING; decode() requires each frame type's TLVs (BCH and SI one SDU, PCCH an SDU and its paging stamp, MSG4 the contention resolution identity and one SDU, ...) and skips a TLV type it does not know. The UE's ideal MAC (src/entity/mac/ue_ideal) runs random access at this level: a random contention preamble in an occasion, the RAR matched by RA-RNTI and RAPID, Msg3 on the TC-RNTI, contention resolution by the first 48 bits of the CCCH SDU, backoff and preambleTransMax. The ideal RLC passes SDUs whole; link impairments are not in P1 (A-02, A-03)

fuzz_uu (P1 N6): the KAIR codec, the PDCP header and a PDCP entity receiving with NIA2/NEA2, and the typed RRC readers with a decode-encode-decode property, 925,527 inputs in 61 s clean from 17 seeds. A first manual run crawled because libFuzzer symbolized each new function in a binary carrying the asn1c RRC library; tools/fuzz.sh already passes -print_funcs=0

NGAP and F1AP builders and readers as built in P1 N7 (src/codec/asn1/msg/{ngap,f1ap}), the RRC route (KS-RRC-B2): a typed struct per message of the P1 sets (ADR 0009 point h without sessions; F1 Setup, the RRC message transfers, UE Context Setup, Modification, Release Request and Release, Paging, Error Indication), inputs checked, built as JER, encoded strictly as APER by the generated code; readers decode APER and read the IEs P1 interprets; peek() reads the procedure, class, criticality and UE IDs of any PDU for the TS 38.413 10 handling. Readers tolerate what other producers send: a user location other than NR leaves cell and TAI unset, an NG SETUP REQUEST from a node other than a gNB is unsupported, never malformed. For the messages P1 builds this closes KS-PLAT-G3: an out-of-constraint value is refused by the strict encoder before it is sent, and received values are read into typed fields, never re-encoded

K_gNB crosses the NGAP codec as octets (the Security Key of INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST, TS 38.413 9.3.1.87): the codec layer holds no SecretBytes (rule R3). The CU-CP copies it into SecretBytes as soon as the request is read and wipes the codec's octets; the JER helpers overwrite every string of a value (the JER text built or read included) before freeing it. asn1c frees its own decode buffers without wiping them. Keys never appear in events or logs; pcap redaction of the Security Key is N8's

The CU-CP as built in P1 N7 (src/proc/ran/cucp). Choices: (1) one DU and one AMF; IDs [shard:4][gen:4][index:24] with shard 0 and generation 0 in P1, the same value as gNB-CU UE F1AP ID and RAN UE NGAP ID; (2) NG Setup waits for the DU's F1 Setup (its TAs come from the cell) and is redone when NG-C comes back, after a failure's time to wait; NG-C loss releases the UEs that had an AMF; (3) INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP: UE CONTEXT SETUP to the DU for SRB2 first, then the AS SMC with the first of 128-NEA2, NEA1 (NEA0 only with the D1 bisect switch) and 128-NIA2, NIA1 the UE supports, a capability enquiry only when the request carries no UE radio capability (then UE RADIO CAPABILITY INFO INDICATION), RRCReconfiguration with SRB2, the masterCellGroup and the NAS PDU, and the response on its complete; an AS SMC failure shows as an SRB1 integrity failure of the unprotected SecurityModeFailure and answers INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP FAILURE; (4) TS 38.413 10: an undecodable PDU gets ERROR INDICATION transfer-syntax-error, a procedure outside P1 with criticality reject abstract-syntax-error-reject, a P1 message missing an IE abstract-syntax-error-falsely-constructed-message, an unknown RAN UE NGAP ID unknown-local-UE-NGAP-ID, a mismatched AMF UE NGAP ID inconsistent-remote-UE-NGAP-ID; (5) a key change by UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION is P3 (acknowledged); AMF STATUS INDICATION is an event only

The control path in virtual time (tests/procedure/ran_test.cpp, P1 N7): a UE (5GMM, RRC, soft card) over KAIR to the DU, F1 over memlink to the CU-CP, NG-C over memlink to the core stub's AMF (NAS and NGAP sides). Ten tests: F1 then NG Setup; registration with NIA2/NEA2 at AS, the capability enquiry reported to the AMF, no stub verdict failed at NAS or NGAP level; de-registration ending in a release through F1; paging by 5G-S-TMSI reaching the idle UE; ERROR INDICATION for an undecodable PDU, an unknown RAN UE NGAP ID and a PDU SESSION RESOURCE SETUP REQUEST from the external corpus (criticality reject, outside P1); NG RESET releasing the UEs; AMF CONFIGURATION UPDATE acknowledged. In the mutants preset kgnb_wrong_ul_count is killed end to end: the UE's AS SMC fails and the stub records INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP FAILURE. fuzz_ngap_proc (hostile NG-C into a CU-CP with a cell, seeded from the 108 NGAP corpus vectors) ran 41,113 inputs in 61 s clean (L15)

Builder and reader checks of P1 N7: oracle.py builders now covers 64 samples (RRC 21, NGAP 26, F1AP 17), each PASS in pycrate, tshark and asn1c. Two first NGAP samples and one F1AP sample nested invalid payloads (a REGISTRATION ACCEPT without its result, a UE radio capability that was not UERadioAccessCapabilityInformation, the broadcast BCCH messages where F1AP's gNB-DU System Information wants the bare MIB and SIB1) and were corrected, adding rrc::radio_access_capability, mib_ie and sib1_ie. The external corpora read as P1's readers see them: NGAP 70 vectors read and 23 outside the P1 set, F1AP 16 read and 6 outside, none malformed
evidence: tests/unit/asn1/ngap_msg_test.cpp; tests/unit/asn1/f1ap_msg_test.cpp; tests/oracles/oracle.py builders; P1 N7

summary: The DU as built in P1 N7 (src/proc/ran/du): one TDD cell (n78, SCS 30 kHz, 106 PRBs as F1 Setup states them; no PHY behind them, A-01); F1 Setup with the MIB and SIB1 as gNB-DU System Information, retried after a failure's time to wait; MIB every 80 ms and SIB1 every 160 ms once the CU activates the cell; one RAR per PRACH, the same TC-RNTI for UEs on the same preamble and occasion within 10 ms, the first Msg3 winning and getting Msg4 once the CU's RRCSetup arrives, later ones none (their UEs time out and retry); SRB PDUs carried as RRC containers; UE Context Setup and Modification adding SRBs with LCID = SRB ID and answering with the CellGroupConfig of the new RLC bearers; UE Context Release sending its RRC container before the context goes; Paging stamped with PF = UE_ID mod 128 (T = 128, N = T, i_s 0) but sent at once (A-11). F1 loss drops the cell and its UEs

memlink (P1 N2) could reorder a direction on real-time shards: it turned its monotonic due time into a delay from one clock reading, and Shard::start_timer added that delay to a later reading, so a tick in between put a message a millisecond past the next one, whose due time equalled the recorded one. Seen once in the N7 full CI (AssocContract over two Shards under ASan and parallel load: 0-6, 8, 9, 7). Fixed with TimerService::start_timer_at (an absolute deadline, ties in start order) used by both memlink paths; a conformance test on SimLoop and Shard; 96 parallel ASan runs of the contract clean

The UE's NAS security context (P1 N4) used BEARER 0 for NAS integrity and ciphering. TS 33.501 6.4.3.1 and 6.4.4.1 make BEARER the NAS connection identifier, which 6.4.2.1 sets to 0x01 for 3GPP access (0x02 non-3GPP). The core stub shares proc/ue/nas_sec, and the test vectors of tests/unit/proc/nas_sec_test.cpp had been computed outside the code but with the same reading, so nothing local could see it; the first Open5GS runs (P1 N8) did: every SECURITY MODE COMMAND failed the UE's MAC check (event nas.sec.discard verdict=discard_mac) after RES* had verified. Fixed (kBearer3gpp = 1); the vectors recomputed with BEARER 1 by the same Python cryptography route, which reproduces the old values with BEARER 0; then 9/9 N8 rows passed on Open5GS. The class of defect the Open5GS control exists for (ADR 0005, ADR 0010)

The DU's default NR cell identity (P1 N7) was 0x1A0000001, whose leftmost 22 bits are 0x6800, not the gNB ID 0x1A0 (TS 38.300 8.2: NCI = gNB ID || local cell ID). Fixed: the default is 0x1A0 << 14 | 1, and the all-in-one node derives the NCI from the topology's gNB ID and length; Open5GS logged CELL_ID 0x680001 for the UEs' user location

The core stub's AMF (P1 N5) did not release the UE's N2 context after a switch-off DEREGISTRATION REQUEST: TS 24.501 5.5.2.2.2 sends no accept, but TS 23.502 4.2.2.3.2 step 8 still has the AMF release the signalling connection. Seen in the first real-time component run (the RAN kept the UE's context). Fixed in tests/corestub/amf.cpp; the procedure test now expects the network release

The all-in-one node as built in P1 N8 (src/node/aio, ADR 0009): one real-time shard runs the DU, the CU-CP and the UE farm, the NG-C SCTP association on its reactor (the [shard:4][gen:4][index:24] routing and an SCTP I/O thread wait for a second shard); F1 over memlink as encoded F1AP; the air link as encoded KAIR v1 frames over memlink datagrams; NG-C over real SCTP, never memory (architecture 2.1). Each UE is a node::UeDevice: its card from cards/usim-5g.yaml, personalised by the sim-range identity rule (ICCID 8988211 00 || MSIN, MSISDN 999 || the MSIN's last 8 digits) and given its sealed secrets; power on reads the card and registers once 5GMM leaves 5GMM-NULL; a switch-off leaves the device off. The topology YAML is the P1 subset of architecture 9 (one AMF, one gNB, one DU, one cell, UE groups of a sim range, S-NSSAIs as SST or SST-SD; the gNB announces every slice its UEs ask for), unknown keys refused. The control API's threads reach the procedures only by posting to the shard and waiting (5 s, else exit 7)

The control API as built in P1 N8 (src/api, ADR 0009 point 7): HTTP/1.1 and JSON by cpp-httplib (vendored) on <run>/ctl.sock, optionally TCP on a loopback address only; every answer {exit, kv} with cli.md's exit codes as HTTP statuses (src/api/openapi.yaml). A root helper on /run/ksim/netd.sock (SOCK_SEQPACKET, the socket 0666 since SO_PEERCRED decides: one uid is served). Requests are a small binary format (version, op, length-prefixed fields; at most 1024 octets; a trailing octet is malformed): setup_node <netns> <parent> <addr>/<prefix>, teardown, socket <netns> sctp|udp v4|v6, list, gc. The policy: names ^ksim-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ up to 31 characters; a parent only the configured one, and none unless the host is kaluza-uesim (none on the dev PC); addresses only in the configured range (172.30.30.30-.39/24 in the lab); only namespaces netd lists may be torn down or have sockets made. setup_node makes a named namespace as iproute2 keeps them (a bind mount on /run/netns/<name>, made shared), lo up, and with a parent an L2 ipvlan 'ksim0' created straight into the namespace (IFLA_NET_NS_FD) carrying the address; a failure half way removes the namespace. socket makes the socket on a thread that joined the namespace and passes it over SCM_RIGHTS. ksim with a topology netd: section has netd make its CU-CP namespace and takes every NG-C socket from it through SctpClient's SocketSource; a socket keeps its namespace, so ksim binds and connects it in its own and never calls setns; the namespace goes at stop, and one left by a run that died is replaced

PDU sessions at the CU-CP as built in P1 N10 (src/proc/ran/cucp; TS 38.413 8.2, TS 37.483 8.3, TS 38.473 8.3.4, TS 38.331 5.3.5). One session procedure at a time per UE, queued: a PDU SESSION RESOURCE SETUP REQUEST, or the sessions of an INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST after its first reconfiguration (the ICS response then carries them), gets one DRB per session, the session's default DRB with every flow on it (DRB IDs from 1, the lowest free); the CU-UP's bearer context by BEARER CONTEXT SETUP (K_UPenc and K_UPint from K_gNB, TS 33.501 A.8, for the AS algorithms in use; wiped once encoded) or by MODIFICATION to add; the DU's DRB by UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION with the CU-UP's F1-U uplink end; the DU's F1-U downlink end back to the CU-UP by MODIFICATION; then RRCReconfiguration with the DRB (SDAP header both ways, PDCP 18-bit SNs), the DU's cell group and the session's NAS PDU, and the response with the CU-UP's N3 end once the UE completes it. UP security: ciphering always (D1), integrity only when the session's policy says required, never for preferred (ADR 0009 point b). A PSI the UE already holds, or twice in one request, is answered as failed with multiple-PDU-session-ID-instances (F-26); no CU-UP, no E1 or no AS keys fails the request cleanly. A release reconfigures the UE first (the DRB and the NAS PDU), then releases the DRB at the DU and the session at the CU-UP (or the whole bearer context with the last session), then answers; a UE context release also releases the E1 bearer context

Not built: PDU SESSION RESOURCE MODIFY INDICATION (nothing in P2 triggers it: no dual connectivity, no CU-UP relocation); a GTP-U ERROR INDICATION received on N3 or F1-U is reported as an event and not acted on (the session is not released); dynamic 5QIs and IPv6 transport are refused as unsupported by the codec. GBR flows are built in P2 Q11 (KS-RRC-B7). Until P2 Q10 a PDU SESSION RESOURCE MODIFY REQUEST was only acknowledged and NOTIFY was not built; both are now (KS-NGAP-B9)

The gNB-CU-UP as built in P1 N10 (src/proc/ran/cuup): E1 SETUP sent when its association comes up (PPID 64); a bearer context per UE with a PDCP entity per DRB on the gNB side (18-bit SNs, the SDAP header both ways), the N3 tunnel per session and an F1-U uplink tunnel per DRB, TEIDs tagged 0x31 (N3) and 0x32 (F1-U) in their top octet. Downlink: N3 G-PDU with the DL PDU Session Container, the flow's DRB by QFI, SDAP header, PDCP (ciphered; integrity only when the session asked for it), F1-U G-PDU with the NR-U DL USER DATA header and its sequence number. Uplink: F1-U G-PDU, PDCP, the SDAP header's QFI, N3 G-PDU with the UL PDU Session Container. A G-PDU for no DRB or before the DU's end is known is dropped and counted

DRBs at the DU as built in P1 N10 (src/proc/ran/du; TS 38.473 8.3, TS 38.321 table 6.2.1-1): UE CONTEXT SETUP and MODIFICATION take DRBs to set up and to release; DRB n gets LCID 3 + n (DRBs 1..29) on an RLC AM bearer in the CellGroupConfig the DU returns, and a released DRB's LCID goes into the cell group's release list; each DRB gets a downlink F1-U tunnel (TEIDs tagged 0x21) delivering its PDCP PDUs to the UE on that LCID, and uplink SDUs on a DRB's LCID go to the CU-UP's F1-U end as plain G-PDUs; a UE released or lost takes its tunnels with it. The F1AP DRB IEs (DRBs to be set up and set up, the S-NSSAI, the flows with 5QI and ARP, the UL and DL UP TNL information) are P1's subset: IPv4, non-GBR, no E-UTRAN QoS (an OCUDU sample with E-UTRAN QoS and IPv6 is correctly unsupported)

The GTP-U endpoint as built in P1 N10 (src/entity/gtpu; TS 29.281 j00): one UDP port, tunnels by local TEID with an 8-bit tag in the top octet naming the owner (0x21 DU F1-U, 0x31 CU-UP N3, 0x32 CU-UP F1-U, 0x51 the stub's UPF) and a 24-bit counter, never 0. A G-PDU carries the PDU Session Container (DL or UL PDU SESSION INFORMATION with the QFI) or the NR-U DL USER DATA header with its sequence number; Echo Request is answered (7.2.2) and one can be sent; a G-PDU for a TEID the endpoint does not know is answered with ERROR INDICATION carrying the TEID and its own address (7.3.1), one received is reported. summary: Radio link supervision and power in the ideal link (P1 N12, ledger A-14): a connected UE sends a KAIR KEEPALIVE every 200 ms; the DU, hearing nothing from a UE for 1 s, sends F1 UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST (rl-failure-others) and the CU-CP NGAP UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST with radio connection with UE lost (L1); the UE, hearing nothing from its cell for 1 s, declares a radio link failure, which goes to the NAS as an RRC connection failure (no re-establishment, A-13). The UE's radio can be switched off and on: off, it hears and sends nothing and leaves its cell; a switch-off keeps it on until the request is out. gnb restart takes the cell off the air for 2 s

Releases and restarts at the gNB and the stub (P1 N12): ksim-ctl gnb ue-release asks the AMF for a release (user-inactivity by default) and is refused while one of the UE's procedures (an INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP, a session's setup or release) is in progress, since such a UE is not inactive; gnb restart rebuilds the DU, CU-CP, CU-UP and their links in place (netd's namespaces, the N3 socket and the air are kept), so the gNB sets up F1, E1 and NG again. ksim-corestub keeps its AMF, with the UE contexts, across a new association (L11): a second NG Setup drops every N2 connection, a returning UE is found by its 5G-S-TMSI or 5G-GUTI; /v1/stub/restart sends AMF STATUS INDICATION and aborts the association 300 ms later

The CU-CP's local release (the NG association lost, an NG RESET) sent F1 UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND without an RRCRelease since P1 N7, so the UE stayed RRC_CONNECTED on bearers the CU-UP had released and its uplink was lost. Found by ksim-p1-restart.sh in N12 (row amf-ueransim.069 failed after the AMF restart); the RRCRelease on SRB1 now goes in the command, as in a release the AMF commands

What the UE keeps on the USIM (P1 N12, src/proc/ue/nas_sec/persist; TS 31.102 j60): EF.5GS3GPPLOCI (4F01) as 20 octets, the 5G-GUTI as a 5GS mobile identity IE from its length (all FF without one), the last visited registered TAI (a PLMN of FFFFFF reads as none) and the update status; EF.5GS3GPPNSC (4F03) as a record with the A0 TLV of 4.4.11.4: ngKSI (7 for no valid context), K_AMF, the uplink and downlink NAS COUNTs and the algorithms, padded with FF; EF.5GAUTHKEYS (4F05) as K_AUSF and K_SEAF for 3GPP access in octets 0 to 67 (UST service 133 not available, so the rest is left alone), FF..FF for a key not held. Read at power on (a valid context and the 5G-GUTI make the next registration protected), written through one queue in order: LOCI at every accept, rejects and a new 5G-GUTI, the context marked invalid when an initial registration starts and stored valid on entering 5GMM-DEREGISTERED, the keys after each 5G AKA. A write the card refuses is the event nas.mm.usim_error (none in CI). The layouts with keys live in proc, since codec holds no SecretBytes; the plain buffers are wiped

ksim-netd could not start ping (since P1 N11): its unit's CapabilityBoundingSet (NET_ADMIN, SYS_ADMIN, SETUID, SETGID) is inherited by every command exec starts, and /usr/bin/ping carries cap_net_raw=ep, so the kernel refused to exec it (EPERM: a capability-dumb binary whose file capabilities the bounding set withholds) and the netns ping exited 127 with no packet sent. Found in W1 (2026-10-15 12:44 KST: two sessions up on kaluza-core, no GTP-U on ens19) and reproduced on kaluza-uesim with setpriv; tools/ci.d/67-netns.sh, which would have caught it, SKIPs without KSIM_CI_PRIV. CAP_NET_RAW is now in the bounding set only: the command still drops to the asking user under no-new-privileges, so it gains nothing and ping uses the namespace's ICMP datagram socket. A failed exec now writes its errno to the command's stderr, and ksim-ctl ping reports exit 126/127 as "could not be run" with that line

ksim-ctl ping in netns mode always failed once the ping had run (since P1 N11): the route read RECEIVED as a number (nlohmann::json value with an int64 default) while a reply keeps every value as a string, so the type error ended the handler ("the handler failed") and the ping's counts never reached the gate. Found in W1 (2026-10-15 13:10 KST), where the capture on ens19 showed the echoes answered (3 of 3 from 172.30.61.1, the 1400-octet DF probe answered at 1400, 3 of 3 from the P-CSCF 172.30.63.10 on ims); like KS-PLAT-D7 it hid behind the privileged hook's SKIP. The routes now read a reply's values as text through one out-of-line helper (kv_text; inlined, json's value() and get() trip gcc 15's -Wnull-dereference at -O3)

EAP-AKA' in the UE as built in the P1 N12 follow-up (src/proc/ue/nas_mm, src/codec/nas/eap; TS 24.501 5.4.1.2.2, TS 33.501 6.1.3.1 and Annex F, RFC 5448/9048). Choices: (1) the identity in MK is the IMSI's digits (Annex F.3, SUPI type IMSI); (2) a first AT_KDF other than 1 is an incorrect AUTN, so no KDF negotiation (5.4.1.2.2.12 a); (3) a network name other than this PLMN's SNN, an AUTN the USIM refuses or one without the separation bit gets AKA'-Authentication-Reject; a stale SQN AKA'-Synchronization-Failure with AT_AUTS and a copy of the AT_KDFs (RFC 5448 3.2); an AT_MAC that does not verify, a challenge without RAND, AUTN or MAC, an AKA'-Identity request (Table F.2-1, AT_PERMANENT_REQ) or another method a client error "unable to process packet"; an AKA'-Notification is answered; (4) each error response starts T3520 and pauses T3510/T3521, three in a row and the network failed the check (5.4.1.2.4.5 e); (5) the partial context's K_AMF comes from K_SEAF of EMSK's K_AUSF with the request's ABBA, and that K_AUSF and K_SEAF become the anchor keys only at EAP-success, in the SECURITY MODE COMMAND or an AUTHENTICATION RESULT; EAP-failure deletes them (5.4.1.2.2.8, .11); (6) a malformed EAP packet is discarded (RFC 3748 4.1). The codec keeps no keys: proc computes and checks AT_MAC (constant-time compare). The core stub plays the AUSF with the same rules (profile eap_aka_prime and its faults)

The rest of N12's 5GMM, built in the follow-up: (1) 5.3.20.2 for 3GPP access, the UE taken as in its HPLMN (the sim's subscriptions are home ones) and not configured for T3245: a REGISTRATION or SERVICE REJECT without integrity protection with #3, #6, #7, #11, #12, #13, #15, #27, #31, #36, #62, #72, #73 or #80 stops T3510/T3517 and starts T3247 uniformly in 30-60 min (a keyed draw from the run's seed); #3, #6, #7 keep the USIM valid while the "considered invalid" event counter is under 3 (the UE's maximum; the spec allows up to 10), forbidding the current TA instead; #11, #36, #73 forbid the TA and not the PLMN; #31 is discarded (no CIoT); #62 takes the "should" alternative; T3247's expiry allows those TAs again, makes the USIM valid again under the maximum and registers; (2) #62 keeps the rejected S-NSSAIs out of later Requested NSSAIs until power-off or a UICC removal; #73 is #11 on 3GPP access; #72 on 3GPP access is abnormal; (3) a network de-registration's cause is handled as 5.5.2.3.2 says, with none and no re-registration 5U2, T3502 and ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION (5.5.2.3.4 b); met during the UE's own normal de-registration it is accepted without a new registration (5.5.2.2.6 d), and a CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND then is ignored (e); (4) ksim-ctl ue sim remove de-registers a registered UE (normal, with the 5G-GUTI, nothing written to the absent card), then NO-SUPI with the forbidden lists, the rejected NSSAI and the counters erased; sim insert reads the card again and registers; (5) airplane on is the switch-off de-registration with the radio off, airplane off a power-on

Choices: (1) TC1* 10 s with two retransmissions (5.3.2.1 leaves the value and 1-3 retransmissions to the implementation), TR1M 40 s, TRAM 30 s (10.1); (2) one MO RP transaction at a time; a further one goes in place of the final CP-ACK of the last (5.4); (3) RP-DA is EF.SMSP's TS-Service-Centre-Address (TON/NPI and digits, record 1, 4.2.27); without one it goes empty and the event says so (L7); (4) an MT SMS-DELIVER is stored in the first free EF.SMS record (status 03, the RP-OA, the TPDU) and answered with RP-ACK without a DELIVER-REPORT; with no free record or the memory set full, RP-ERROR #22 and EF.SMSS's flag set, RP-SMMA once available; (5) TP-MR one up from EF.SMSS's last; (6) a text that does not fit one TPDU is cut into parts of 153 septets or 67 UCS2 characters with the 8-bit reference concatenation element, an escaped GSM character never split; (7) SMS-SUBMIT is refused locally (ksim-ctl exit 6) while SMS over NAS is not allowed

The card's APDU trace (uicc/trace, P1 N14; sim-uicc.md section 6). Records are APDUs: an answer of 61xx or 6Cxx is held per channel and merged with the GET RESPONSE (or the command sent again) that follows, the command's Le dropped; a held exchange not followed up goes out as it was. Why: pySim-trace's gsmtap-udp source passes each record to its decoder as a whole APDU, without the T=0 filter its library has, so a SELECT answered 61xx counted as failed and its file state was lost (57 unknown FIDs in a dump). Redaction: CK, IK and Kc in AUTHENTICATE answers (straight or through GET RESPONSE) zeroed with RES kept; PIN command data as 'FF'; reads and writes of the key files (os::key_fid: EF.KEYS, EF.KEYSPS, 4F03, 4F04, 4F05, AF20, AF30) zeroed, by FID or by SFI in the ADF and DF.5GS, an SFI elsewhere in a DF.5x masked when unsure; lengths kept so the record decodes. The selection is followed while the trace is off. On the card side, the ATR goes into the trace only after a reset or power-on: pcscd's vpcd driver polls the ATR to see the card is there, and traced polls made pySim-trace reset its state mid-dump

The UE took a stored 5G NAS security context, once it had protected an initial message with it, for secure exchange on the connection (since P1 N5). Two effects followed. A plain IDENTITY REQUEST for the SUCI was discarded, where TS 24.501 j80 §4.4.4.2 has the UE process it until the network establishes secure exchange. And the UE ciphered its uplink before that point, where §4.4.5 starts ciphering only once secure exchange is established. Found in W2 on kaluza-core: after a switch-off, the AMF had dropped the UE's context, so it could not verify the GUTI-identified, integrity-protected REGISTRATION REQUEST and asked for the SUCI three times per attempt (T3570). The UE discarded each request and gave up on T3510. Fixed in proc/ue/nas_mm: secure_exchange_ lasts one NAS signalling connection, set by the SMC or by a downlink message that passes the integrity check, cleared with the connection. Plain messages are judged by it, and the uplink is ciphered only once it is set (integrity-only before, §4.4.4.1). Test: tests/procedure Identification.* with the stub's forget_on_deregistration

The core stub after W2 (P1 N18). Profile forget_on_deregistration drops the UE's context and 5G-GUTI at its de-registration, as kaluza-core does. With it, a 5G-GUTI the AMF does not know gets a plain IDENTITY REQUEST for the SUCI (§5.4.3). An integrity-only IDENTITY RESPONSE, AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE or FAILURE it cannot check is taken before secure exchange (§4.4.4.3). A request that came protected but could not be verified gets RINMR in the SMC, so the whole message comes back (§5.4.2.2 a); before, the stub expected the container without asking for it. The AUTHENTICATION REQUEST's ngKSI is never the one the UE named (§5.4.1.3.7 c, #71). From N15 the stub also checks that S1 mode and an S1 UE network capability go together (§5.5.1.2.2)

In 5GMM-CONNECTED the UE did not ask for the user plane of a session that had none (since P1 N12): service_request() returned at once when connected, so uplink data waited for bearers that never came. TS 24.501 j80 §5.6.1.1 b covers 5GMM-IDLE and 5GMM-CONNECTED alike. Found on Open5GS (N17 first run) and in W3 on kaluza-core: after a periodic registration both AMFs kept the NAS connection up without user-plane resources, and the ping that follows (row amf-ueransim.039) got nothing. The stub releases the connection after a periodic update, so it never showed. Fixed: in 5GMM-CONNECTED the UE sends SERVICE REQUEST (service type data, Uplink data status) on the connection, protected, with T3517; sessions whose user plane an accepted registration or service request already brings back (up_pending_, cleared when bearers come up or the connection goes) wait instead. The stub answers such a request with the SERVICE ACCEPT as the NAS-PDU of a PDU SESSION RESOURCE SETUP REQUEST (TS 38.413 9.2.1.1). Test: Idle.Ts24501_5_6_1_1_b_*

After a SERVICE REQUEST from 5GMM-IDLE aborted because the RRC connection could not be set up, the UE started another at once whenever a 5GSM message or uplink data was still waiting (Mm::on_released). Seen in LW5d on kaluza-uesim (KS-PLAT-T63): our CU-CP killed, our DU's cell still on without F1, each of 10 UEs with a PDU SESSION RELEASE REQUEST queued sent 475 service requests in 94 s, each failing at random access. TS 24.501 j80 §5.6.1.7 l: on a lower layer failure or release before the procedure completes the UE aborts it, stops T3517, releases its resources locally and enters 5GMM-REGISTERED; only case m) of §5.6.1.1 may be retried, at most 5 times. Fixed: an SR aborted by the release starts nothing more from that release; what waited for it stays queued for the next trigger, an upper layer's request or a 5GSM timer's retransmission (T3582's, here). Test: procedure_idle Ts24501_5_6_1_7_l_And_4_4_3_1_… (one SR in 10 s with no cell, then T3582's SR accepted when the cell is back; before the fix 51 in 10 s)

The UE's uplink NAS COUNT went up for an initial NAS message (a SERVICE REQUEST or a protected REGISTRATION REQUEST) whose RRC connection was never set up, so it never left the UE. TS 24.501 j80 §4.4.3.1: after each new or retransmitted security-protected message the sender increases the NAS COUNT, 'except for the initial NAS messages if the lower layers indicated the failure to establish the RRC connection (see 3GPP TS 38.331)'. Seen in LW5d (KS-PLAT-T63): with KS-NAS-D6's 475 attempts each UE's COUNT reached about 478 while kaluza-core's AMF held about 3, so the first SERVICE REQUEST that reached it carried SN 214..223, the AMF estimated an overflow of 0 and its integrity check failed, correctly (TS 33.501 §6.4.3.1 cannot see a wrap the network never saw); kaluza-core-92 then added F-83. Fixed: RRC tells NAS that the connection was never established (TS 38.331 §5.3.3.7: T300, RRCReject, a failed random access) before the release, and the COUNT the initial message took is given back. nas.sr.request from 5GMM-IDLE now names the COUNT it took. The split run's supervisor as built in P2 Q3 (apps/ksim/supervisor, ADR 0011 point 1). ksim run with a mode: split topology starts the CU-CP, CU-UP, DU and UE farm as this same program with --role, in that order, each in <run>/<role>/ with its output in <run>/<role>.out, and takes each as up when it prints CTL=. It follows every role's /v1/events and relays them into its own ring and events.ndjson (EventRing::relay, a new seq, the role's own t_ms), so wait sees the whole run. It serves <run>/ctl.sock and passes each call to the role that owns it (UE verbs to the farm, gNB verbs to the CU-CP, du and cuup verbs to theirs); info, nodes, wait, events and stop are its own; gnb ue-release asks the farm for the UE's C-RNTI and the CU-CP to release it. gnb restart stops and starts the DU, CU-UP and CU-CP processes; cucp|du|cuup <name> restart one of them; a restarted role's last directory is kept as <role>.<n>/. A role that ends on its own is reported as run.role.exit. <run>/<capture>.pcapng links to the role that writes it (ngap, f1ap, e1ap: the CU-CP; gtpu: the CU-UP; uu, sim: the farm)

NR-U DL DATA DELIVERY STATUS as built in P2 Q4 (TS 38.425 5.4.2, 5.5.2.2). The DU sends it on the CU-UP's UL tunnel, in a G-PDU of its own with no T-PDU: the initial one the moment a DRB is set up (5.4.2.1: the UE is on the cell already; a CU-UP may hold DL data until it has a buffer size, as OCUDU's does, and the core sends buffered DL data as soon as the tunnel is up), one at once for a DL USER DATA with Report Polling (with the polled frame's NR-U SN), and otherwise one 10 ms after DL data. It reports a desired buffer of 8 MiB and, the DRBs being RLC AM over the ideal link, the highest DL PDCP SN sent to the UE as both highest delivered and highest transmitted (none before the first PDU). Our CU-UP counts the reports (cuup bearers DDDS_RX) and does not obey them (ledger: the DU's buffer is ideal); a report never reaches PDCP as data. The GTP-U entity carries the Report Polling flag and the frame both ways

The CU-CP's UP security policy (P2 Q9; TS 38.413 8.2.1.2, TS 33.501 6.6.1; proc/ran/up_security). A Security Indication's "required" is performed. Integrity this gNB cannot do (up_policy.integrity_possible false) refuses the session in PDU Session Resource Setup Unsuccessful, radioNetwork up-integrity-protection-not-possible; ciphering always can. "preferred" is performed as the local policy says (preferred_integrity, preferred_confidentiality, both true by default, as OCUDU's CU-CP does) and reported in the Security Result, which goes back only then (9.3.1.59). "not-needed" is not performed. With no Security Indication (38.413 leaves the case open; kaluza-core's SMF sends none) the local default applies: integrity off, ciphering on (absent_integrity, absent_confidentiality), as OCUDU's. The policy is a topology setting, cucp {up_policy: {...}}, and ksim-ctl gnb <name> up-policy changes it at run time for the sessions after. Every decision is a ran.up.security event (indication present or absent, what was asked, what was done, set-up or the refusal's cause). The stub's AMF takes a refusal with either UP security cause. This replaces KS-NGAP-B5's "integrity when required, never when preferred".

The CU-CP's QoS flow to DRB mapping is a topology setting (P2 Q10; ADR 0011; TS 38.300 12, TS 37.324 5.3): gnbs[].cucp {drb_map: per-5qi | per-session}, default per-5qi. per-5qi gives each 5QI of a session its own DRB; the DRB of the session's first flow is the default DRB, as OCUDU's CU-CP does. per-session puts every flow of the session on one DRB, P1's way. A modification keeps the mapping: an added flow joins its 5QI's DRB or gets a new one; a flow whose 5QI changes moves to that 5QI's DRB; a DRB left with no flow is removed. DRB IDs are 1..29 per UE, since the DU gives DRB n LCID n+3 (TS 38.321 LCIDs 4..32); a flow with no free ID fails with radio-resources-not-available. ksim-ctl gnb <name> qos <ue> shows each session's DRBs with their QFIs and 5QI.

summary: PDU SESSION RESOURCE MODIFY end to end at the CU-CP (P2 Q10; TS 38.413 8.2.3, 8.2.4). It is a UE job like a setup, queued behind any procedure the UE has running. Each session's change is planned first (flows released, then added or modified, and the AMBR). Then E1 sets up, remaps and removes the CU-UP's DRBs and gives the DL session-AMBR. F1 sets up, modifies and releases the DU's DRBs. The DU's F1-U ends of new DRBs go back over E1. Then one RRCReconfiguration carries the new DRBs, the changed mappings (no pdcp-Config), the released DRBs, the DU's cell group and the sessions' NAS. The response goes once the UE completes it: the flows added or modified, and the ones that could not be added with radio-resources-not-available. A change with nothing for the radio (the AMBR, a flow's QoS on the same DRB) sends the NAS in DLInformationTransfer. A failure on the way answers every session as failed to modify, and the sessions keep what they had at the CU-CP. A flow released by the gNB itself (ksim-ctl gnb <name> qos-release <ue> --psi N --qfi N) goes the same way and is told in PDU SESSION RESOURCE NOTIFY with radioNetwork release-due-to-ngran-generated-reason. The AMF gets no response for it.

Our CU-CP asked for 2 SCTP streams on NG-C (cucp ng_streams, default 2) and allowed only 2 inbound, so every UE's signalling shared stream 1. TS 38.412 V19.0.0 §7 requires at least one stream pair for UE-associated signalling and says 'a few pairs (i.e. more than one) should be reserved'. Seen in LW5b: kaluza-core's AMF orders N2 turns per (association, stream), so it served our 100 switch-off de-registrations one at a time (09:07:10.269-15.475 KST, about 52 ms each, kaluza-core-92's trace). The AMF then sent a second UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND for each, which our CU-CP answered with an ERROR INDICATION, unknown local UE NGAP ID (§10.6). The default is now 10 each way (Linux SCTP's and OCUDU's), and ng_streams sets the inbound maximum too; the CU-CP already spreads UEs over the negotiated streams (1 + RAN UE NGAP ID mod (n - 1)). summary: The UE's uplink QoS classifier (P2 Q10; TS 24.501 6.2.5.1.1.2, 9.11.4.13, Table 9.11.4.13.1; TS 23.501 5.7.1.5; src/proc/ue/qos_classifier). The session's signalled QoS rules are tried in increasing precedence value; a rule without one comes last. The first rule with a packet filter for the uplink (uplink only or bidirectional) whose every component matches gives the QFI. Local is the UE's end and remote the far end: in the uplink the source and the destination, in the downlink the other way round (the stub's UPF classifies downlink with the same code). Components: IPv4 addresses with mask and IPv6 with prefix, protocol or next header after the IPv6 extension headers, TCP/UDP/SCTP ports single and ranged (none in a later fragment), the SPI of ESP and AH, type of service or traffic class with mask, the flow label, and for Ethernet frames the MAC addresses and ranges, the outermost C-TAG and S-TAG VID and PCP/DEI (plain and extended) and the ethertype. A component the packet cannot have does not match. A packet no rule matches is not sent, counted per session (UL_UNMATCHED), with ue.qos.unmatched once. A session without signalled rules sends on its default QFI. The UE now keeps the QoS flow descriptions' 5QI too (create, delete, modify). ksim-ctl ue <sel> ps-list shows the rules, the flows and the UL packets per QFI, and ue.qos.classified tells each rule's first packet.
evidence: src/proc/ue/qos_classifier.cpp; src/proc/ue/nas_sm/sm.cpp; src/node/ue/device.cpp; tests/unit/proc QosClassifier; P2 Q10

summary: The core stub's QoS flows (P2 Q10; tests/corestub/smf, upf). A session can have flows beside the default one, each with its QoS rule (precedence, a packet filter, a direction) and its flow description (5QI). They come from the profile (session: {flows: [...]}), from ksim-ctl stub qos flows-add for the sessions set up after it, or at run time from stub qos add|del --ue SUPI --psi N. add|del is a network-requested modification: a 5GSM MODIFICATION COMMAND creating or deleting the rule and the flow description, inside a PDU SESSION RESOURCE MODIFY REQUEST with the flow to add or release (TS 23.502 4.3.3.2). A session-AMBR change now goes to the gNB too. Filters are written as all, remote=A/N, local=A/N, proto=N, lport=N, lports=N-M, rport=N, rports=N-M, spi=N and tos=V/M. When the gNB answers, the UPF takes the session's rules. It then checks every uplink packet's QFI against its own classification of it (a verdict when they differ), marks each downlink packet with the QFI its downlink filters give, and counts both ways per QFI (UPF_UL_QFI.n, UPF_DL_QFI.n). The AMF takes PDU SESSION RESOURCE NOTIFY: the SMF has the UE delete the released flows' rules, with a 5GSM command alone.

GBR admission at the CU-CP (P2 Q11; ledger A-07; TS 38.413 8.2.1.2, 8.2.3.2, 8.2.4). The cell has a GBR budget, the sum of the admitted flows' GFBR UL plus DL: gnbs[].cucp {gbr_budget_kbps: N}, default 100000, and ksim-ctl gnb <name> gbr-budget [kbps] at run time. A GBR flow that the budget would not cover is refused with radioNetwork radio-resources-not-available, in the setup's QoS Flow Failed to Setup List or the modify's failed list. A session with no flow left fails. A GBR flow always gets a DRB of its own, whatever drb_map says. When the budget changes, or a release or modification frees or takes GFBR, the GBR flows are reassessed in the order the CU-CP holds them. Each is fulfilled while the budget covers it beside those before it. A change in a flow with notification control goes to the AMF in PDU SESSION RESOURCE NOTIFY, as not fulfilled or fulfilled again. ksim-ctl gnb <name> qos shows each DRB's GFBR and the flows not fulfilled. The DU and the CU-UP keep the GFBR F1 and E1 gave them. Nothing schedules by it on the ideal link.

summary: SDAP end-markers and reflective mapping at the UE (P2 Q11; TS 37.324 5.3.1, 5.3.2, 6.2.3). Once a session's SDAP entity is established (after the RRCReconfiguration that made it), two kinds of mapping change send an end-marker control PDU. A flow whose mapping is new sends it on the default DRB. A flow whose mapping moves sends it on the old DRB, when that DRB has a UL SDAP header. Two things change a mapping: an RRCReconfiguration (mappedQoS-FlowsToAdd, including a mapping-only DRB-ToAddMod) and a DL data PDU with the RDI (reflective mapping, which the UE honours). Our CU-UP never sets the RDI. It counts each end-marker it receives and tells it in ran.cuup.end_marker. The UE tells each one it sends in rrc.sdap.end_marker.

summary: Reflective QoS at the UE (P2 Q11; TS 24.501 6.2.5.1.1.3, 6.2.5.1.4). The establishment request carries the 5GSM capability, RqoS set by default or as the persona's phone sent it (nas.sm_capability). The accept's or a modification's RQ timer value sets T3583 for the session: deactivated or zero revokes reflective QoS and drops the derived rules, and none given leaves the default of 1 minute. A DL packet whose SDAP header has the RQI derives a packet filter for UL direction. The filter is built for IPv4 and IPv6 TCP or UDP: remote and local address at full length, protocol, and the ports, swapped from the DL packet. ESP gives none, since no uplink IPsec SA is known, and then the RQI is ignored (6.2.5.1.4.6). A filter not yet held makes a derived rule (precedence 80, the packet's QFI). One already held gets T3583 again and takes the packet's QFI. T3583's expiry removes the rule. The classifier tries the derived rules at precedence 80 among the signalled ones. A DL packet on a QFI the UE has no rule, derived rule or flow description for is discarded and counted (KS-SDAP-002). The derivation runs before that check, so an RQI can bring a new QFI. Events ue.qos.derived, ue.qos.derived_expired and ue.sdap.unknown_qfi; ksim-ctl ue ps-list shows DERIVED, RQ_TIMER_MS, DL_QFI.n and DL_UNKNOWN_QFI.

summary: The core stub for QoS II (P2 Q11; tests/corestub). The SMF sends the RQ timer (profile rq_timer_s, default 60; stub qos rq-timer --seconds N, 0 none) in the accept to a UE that offered RqoS, and counts those sessions (SM_RQOS). Flows can be GBR: --gfbr and --mfbr in kbit/s (the same both ways), --notify for notification control, in N2's GBR QoS Flow Information and the flow description's GFBR/MFBR parameters. stub qos mod --qfi N --5qi N changes a flow where it is. A setup answered with flows not admitted makes the SMF delete their rules at the UE (TS 23.502 4.3.2.2.1). The AMF counts NOTIFY's fulfilled and not-fulfilled entries. stub udp-ue sends a UDP datagram from the DN to the UE's port 7 on a QFI of the test's, with the RQI when asked. The UE's inject mode echoes it (RFC 862). For a datagram sent with the RQI, the UPF expects the reply on its QFI (the UE's derived rule) and records a verdict when it differs.

The performance harness (P2 Q12; requirements.md §3.5, ADR 0011 design point d): tools/perf/perf.sh on one host against ksim-corestub on loopback, from the release build. The UEs are in namespaces of their own and the stub's UPF forwards to a DN namespace (ksim-corestub --dn-netd: netd's setup_dn and dn_tun, dn0 at 10.60.0.1 with a route to the UE pool), where iperf3 servers run; both come from the host's ksim-netd, which needs --dn (lab.md). The method: the link delay at 0 (§3.5 excludes it), t-Reordering 100 ms, headers-only user-plane capture, iperf3 TCP for 10 s; latency is half the ping RTT through the whole user plane, an upper bound for one direction. tools/perf/perf_report.py scores each target and prints the -T row text; build/perf/last holds the numbers and the report. summary: The ideal link's in-memory hops are a topology setting (P2 Q12; architecture §5): link: {delay_ms: N, jitter_ms: M}, by default 1 ms and no jitter, as before; the manifest records it. Each memlink hop (KAIR, F1-C, E1 and F1-U in all-in-one) adds it, so the UE-to-DN path of an aio run had 2 ms each way: a 3.8 ms ping RTT and TCP windows the perf runs could not grow. The performance runs set 0. A message that is due now, with none still waiting in a timer on that end, is delivered in the posted task itself rather than through a timer (in order; a seeded jitter that puts some at 0 still keeps them in order behind those in timers).

In split mode, TCP through the user plane stalled within a second (found by the P2 Q12 harness: iperf3 never finished). The UDP sockets of F1-U and N3 had the kernel's default 212 KB buffers, and loopback dropped datagrams in bursts. In 3 s the DU took 3182 UL SDUs from the UE and the CU-UP got 2960. Below PDCP nothing retransmits (the ideal RLC does not), and t-Reordering defaults to infinity, so the CU-UP's PDCP waited for the hole for good. Fixed: the UDP sockets ask for 8 MB to receive and 4 MB to send (capped by net.core.{r,w}mem_max); the same run then lost nothing (474772 SDUs at the DU, 474763 at the CU-UP, the rest signalling). The perf topologies also set t-Reordering 100 ms, so a hole costs time, not the run. The gates' runs never showed it: their traffic is a few pings.

The core stub's UPF kept every check it made, passes included, with a detail string built for each, about four per uplink packet: under the P2 Q12 harness the stub grew to 1.2 GiB in a minute. It now counts the passes, keeps the failures (all anything reads), and builds a detail only for a failure: 17 MiB after the same run.

A plain kill of the PID `ksim-ctl netd exec` prints left the command running (found by kaluza-core's session: 412 netd helpers, each waiting on an iperf3 server from the P2 Q12 harness). The PID is netd's exec helper, the leader of the command's process group, which waits on the command and reports its status. The helper came with netd's own SIGTERM and SIGINT handlers, which only flag a stop, so the signal did nothing. The helper now passes SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP on to the command, and the harness stops the whole group (kill -TERM -PID; its first version wrote kill -- -PID, which dash's kill refuses, and left the servers again: fixed in P2 Q14 prep). ksim itself always stopped the group and never leaked.

Three P2 gates scored, or aborted on, rows that are not their core's when the whole P2 set ran against a real core (found in P2 Q13 on the Open5GS rig). ksim-p2-card.sh scored the PC/SC row with the topology's in-process card (FAIL), ksim-p2-up.sh scored the absent-Security-Indication row though the rig's SMF sends one (preferred/preferred; FAIL), and ksim-p2-e1.sh aborted outside the stub. CI runs those gates only against the stub, so none showed there. Each now SKIPs with the reason: the card is in process; the core sends an indication, recorded with what it asked for; the row is the stub's.

Our gNB ended NG with an ABORT on every stop (found by kaluza-core-92 in LW1b: the association went COMM_LOST with about 2 s of release signalling queued at the AMF, 36 of 100 UEs never got their release, and kaluza-core's race F-77 followed). AllInOne::teardown_gnb began the SHUTDOWN and reset the SCTP client at once, whose destructor aborts; and the run stopped as soon as the UEs had switched off, with the AMF's releases still to come. A stop (ksim-ctl stop, SIGTERM) now first lets the releases under way end: until the DU holds no UE context, its count has not fallen for 3 s, or 10 s are up (AllInOne::drain; in split mode the supervisor asks the DU's role before it stops any role).
